findings.title: `isAccessTokenId` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, which is inverted
findings.description: The guard `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects exactly the token IDs that carry the expected grant. It should use `!equals`. As written, every correctly encoded token ID fails the matcher in `expectCodeToToken`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`, `expectRefresh`, and the device-code expectation, and a token ID with the wrong grant passes.

findings.title: Grant shortcut is read from the wrong offset
findings.description: The encoded format is `<sessionType 2><tokenType 2><grantType 2>:<rawId>`, so the grant shortcut occupies indexes 4–5. `substring(3, 5)` takes the second character of the token type plus the first character of the grant. The comment ("starts at character 4th char") has the same off-by-one. The correct call is `substring(4, 6)`. Even after the inversion is fixed, the matcher would compare the wrong characters.

findings.title: Null check in the `AccessTokenContext` constructor tests `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`
findings.description: The line `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` repeats the `grantType` argument, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. The message also names the wrong field. The argument should be `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: Javadoc says grant shortcuts are about 3 letters, but the encoding fixes them at 2 characters
findings.description: The new `getShortcut()` Javadoc says "usually like 3-letters shortcut". Every implementation in this diff returns 2 characters, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires exactly 6 characters for session, token and grant combined. A contributor following the Javadoc would produce shortcuts that break decoding.

findings.title: `assertEquals` arguments are reversed in the new encoder tests
findings.description: The assertions pass the actual value first and the expected constant second, for example `Assert.assertEquals(ctx.getSessionType(), AccessTokenContext.SessionType.TRANSIENT)`. JUnit's signature is `(expected, actual)`, so failure messages will be misleading. The assertions still check the right values.

findings.title: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` import is added to `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` but the new line doesn't use it
findings.description: The new `setAttribute` call uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` and does not reference `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory`. Unless it is used elsewhere in the file (I could not check, since this review is limited to the diff), the import is dead.
